statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail returns below the block threshold because the strong Nasdaq-100 advance included a meaningful intraday pullback before recovering toward session highs.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; the broad upside regime remains strong, while observed intraday retracement argues against a no-reversion path at the assessment cutoff.
headline: Nasdaq rebound stays broad, while an intraday pullback lowers Tail to WATCH
body: The Nasdaq-100 was about 1.7% higher near midday after a roughly 0.5% high-to-low pullback and recovery toward the session high. Technology and semiconductor participation remained strong while volatility, long yields and oil were lower. The two-way move keeps Tail below the block threshold despite high Stress.

lookbackSummary: Published Tail rose from low overnight to 24% around the U.S. open, eased to 22% at 15:00 UTC, then crossed to 26% at 16:00 UTC as broad upside alignment persisted.
outlookSummary: Observed midday retracement keeps Tail just below the block threshold. Risk can re-expand into power hour if the recovery becomes one-way; otherwise it should decay after the close, then rise conditionally around Friday Industrial Production, Bowman and the cash open.

forecast.analysis: If midday trade continues to rotate below the highs, Tail should ease as two-way price discovery becomes clearer. A quick recovery that repeatedly rejects pullbacks would keep the regime directional.
Power-hour Tail returns toward upper WATCH if the index holds near highs and pullbacks remain shallow. A balanced closing rotation would keep the risk below the block threshold.
After the cash close, Tail should fall toward lower WATCH if the daytime impulse stops extending. Clean continuation through futures would keep the directional regime active.
Evening Tail falls below WATCH under orderly futures consolidation. A fresh geopolitical or energy shock would be the main route back to a directional risk regime.
Tail remains low if the post-close market stays two-sided and cross-assets remain calmer. Renewed yield or oil pressure could reintroduce directional stress.
Late-evening risk stays low without a new catalyst. Persistent one-way futures extension would invalidate the low-Tail assumption.
Pre-Asia Tail stays low if the U.S. rally consolidates rather than gaps again. A fresh directional gap without retracement would lift risk.
Asia-open Tail remains low under balanced discovery. An abrupt gap or renewed energy escalation would increase directional risk.
Tail stays low if Asian trading remains contained and U.S. futures hold a two-way range. Repeated extension would challenge this base case.
Risk edges higher only if the overnight move becomes directional into the later Asian session; otherwise consolidation keeps Tail low.
Tail remains low if no new macro or geopolitical catalyst disturbs overnight balance. Cross-asset instability would raise uncertainty first.
Europe pre-open can reintroduce modest directional risk if yields or oil move sharply. Stable cross-assets keep Tail below WATCH.
European opening flows can widen the range, but Tail stays low unless the Nasdaq futures path becomes persistently one-way.
Morning European trade carries moderate Stress as U.S. futures position for Friday data. Tail remains low unless directional efficiency strengthens.
Tail stays just below WATCH while markets approach the U.S. session. A one-way premarket move with weak pullbacks would raise risk.
Pre-U.S. positioning raises Stress, but Tail remains low absent persistent mean-reversion failure. The next major checkpoints are still several hours away.
Tail enters WATCH if premarket direction becomes more efficient. Balanced futures rotation would keep the move contained despite rising event proximity.
Risk stays at lower WATCH as markets approach Industrial Production and the cash open. Future escalation remains conditional on actual price-path persistence.
Tail rises within WATCH as the 13:15 UTC Industrial Production release and 13:30 UTC Bowman/cash-open cluster approaches. Event importance lifts Stress more than Tail before outcomes are known.
drivers: 13:30 UTC Bowman speech and cash open

forecast.analysis: The data-and-open hour reaches upper WATCH conditionally. Tail would cross the block threshold only if the observed post-release path shows persistent extension, shallow pullbacks or repeated failed retracements.
Post-open Tail remains elevated within WATCH while price discovery is assessed. Orderly retracements would reduce risk quickly; continued extreme-holding would keep it high.
Late-morning Tail eases if the opening impulse becomes two-sided. Renewed extension with aligned technology breadth would keep the trend risk elevated.
By midday, Tail should drift toward lower WATCH if the morning event impulse has been absorbed. A delayed directional second leg would prevent further decay.

forecastDetail.comment: Current WATCH reflects a strong broad rally, but the observed intraday pullback and recovery show meaningful two-way movement rather than a clean no-retracement path.
Midday risk eases if rotation continues; repeated rejection of pullbacks would keep Tail directional.
Power-hour WATCH is conditional on high-retention and shallow pullbacks; balanced closing trade lowers risk.
Post-close Tail declines if the cash-session impulse stops extending into futures.
Evening risk falls below WATCH under orderly consolidation; a new geopolitical or energy shock would reverse that.
Two-way futures trade and stable yields/oil keep Tail low in the late evening.
